title: Confidence Funnel and Dynamic Probe Gating — Eval-Orchestrator Playbook
author: Asha Menon
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the Confidence Funnel pattern and the Dynamic Probe Gating policy used by the eval-orchestrator to allocate probe budget, prioritize slices, and reduce alert noise while preserving sensitivity to real regressions. It is intended for ML engineers, evaluators, and platform SREs responsible for promotion gating and longtail monitoring.

Problem statement:
- Continuous eval pipelines send a high volume of probes across many slices; naive thresholds lead to alert spam or missed regressions.
- We need a structured, auditable policy that tunes sampling intensity based on observed model confidence and probe signal.

Goals:
- Maintain detection precision >= 0.85 for high-severity regressions (policy target).
- Maintain mean probe cost per model per day below configured budget (default $250/day).
- Reduce low-signal alerts by 60% versus fixed-threshold gating.

Key concepts

1) Confidence Funnel (CF): a tiered decision flow that assigns probes to bands based on model response confidence, recent drift, and slice criticality. Bands:
- Band A (investigate immediately): low confidence (<0.40) OR degraded anchor coverage OR safety sentinel fails. High-urgency; 100% probe retention + human review.
- Band B (fast follow-up): medium-low confidence [0.40,0.65) and trending down; adaptive resample rate x2 for 4 hours.
- Band C (routine scan): confidence [0.65,0.90); periodic sampling at baseline rate.
- Band D (safety-maintenance): confidence >= 0.90 and no telemetry anomalies; sparse sampling (0.5x baseline).

2) Dynamic Probe Gating (DPG): runtime policy that adjusts sampling fraction and probe routing based on CF band, SLO deficit, and available eval budget. DPG enforces:
- Minimum detectability: ensure a slice has at least N=30 probes in the last 24h if it is Band A or critical customer slice.
- Budget-aware throttling: if daily budget burn rate > 90%, reduce Band D sampling first.
- Hedged sampling: for ambiguous slices (confidence 0.45–0.55) route duplicated probes to two different model variants to increase signal fidelity.

When to use

- New model promotions, quantized rollouts, A/B experiments, or customer-facing feature changes.
- Ongoing continuous monitoring where probe volume and slice cardinality are moderate-to-high.

Roles & ownership

- Eval-Orchestrator Team: implements DPG runtime and provides metrics. (Owner: Eval-Orchestrator)
- Model Onboarding / Applied ML Team: defines critical slices, anchor prompts, and probe families. (Owner: Model Onboarding)
- Incident Response / SRE: integrates alerts to oncall and defines remediation runbooks.

SLOs and thresholds

| Metric | Target | Alert threshold | Responsible |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Detection precision (high-sev) | >= 0.85 | < 0.80 for 3h | Applied ML
| Avg probes per model / day | <= $250 (cost) | > $300 (3d rolling) | Eval-Orchestrator
| Probe coverage (critical slices) | >= 95% | < 90% | Model Onboarding
| False positive alert rate | <= 12% | > 20% | SRE/Applied ML

Configuration examples

Example gating policy (YAML):

policy_id: cf-default-2026
banding:
  - name: Band A
    confidence_max: 0.40
    min_probes_24h: 30
    retain: true
  - name: Band B
    confidence_min: 0.40
    confidence_max: 0.65
    resample_multiplier: 2
    window_hours: 4
  - name: Band C
    confidence_min: 0.65
    confidence_max: 0.90
    baseline_sample: 1.0
  - name: Band D
    confidence_min: 0.90
    baseline_sample: 0.5
budgeting:
  daily_usd_cap: 250
  burn_rate_scale: 0.9

DPG runtime decision pseudocode:

1. Ingest probe result R with fields: slice_id, confidence_score, telemetry_flags, timestamp.
2. Map confidence_score to CF band.
3. If telemetry_flags include safety_fail OR slice criticality == high -> promote to Band A.
4. If Band A -> ensure retention and create high-priority task for human review.
5. Else consult budget: if projected_daily_burn > daily_usd_cap * burn_rate_scale -> reduce Band D sampling by 80%.
6. Log decision with trace-id and metric tags: cf_band, sample_fraction, budget_headroom.

Runtime telemetry & graphs to surface

- CF band distribution over time (per-model, per-slice)
- Daily probe cost burn and projected end-of-day spend
- Band transition heatmap (how slices migrate across bands in last 72h)
- Hedged-sample agreement rate (fraction of hedged duplicated probes with matching label)
- Alert signal-to-noise (alerts accepted by humans / alerts triggered)

Alerting and operator flow

Primary alerts (wired to eval-oncall):
1) Detection precision drop: trigger when detection precision < 0.80 for 3h (pager).
2) Budget overrun: projected burn > daily cap*1.10 (page on-call finance liaison).
3) Critical-slice coverage loss: critical slice probe count < min_probes_24h (email + slack channel).

Operator runbook (short):
1. Acknowledge alert and check CF band distribution dashboard.
2. For precision drops: run hedged-replay for top-10 affected slices (see commands below).
3. If hedged-replay confirms regression, escalate to Applied ML and open regression ticket with artifacts: sample probes, model versions, kernel profile.
4. For budget alerts: temporarily throttle Band D via DPG admin UI and notify stakeholders.

Example commands

# run hedged replay for a slice (CLI)
redwood-eval replay --slice-id SLC-2025-42 --window 24h --variants base,quantized --output /tmp/replay-2026.json

# query band distribution (PromQL example)
sum by (cf_band, model) (rate(eval_probe_count[1h]))

Quality & regression triage integration

- Tie CF/DPG metadata into regression triage: every regression incident must include the CF band history and the DPG decisions for the preceding 48h. This reduces attribution ambiguity.
- When promoting model variants, run a promotion-blocking gate that requires: no Band A slices, hedged-agreement >= 0.9 on calibration set, and quantized-avg-latency < latency-SLO + 10%.

Operational considerations and caveats

- Cold-starts: new slices with insufficient history default to Band B with an elevated sampling multiplier for first 6h.
- Adversarial probes: apply rate-limiting and miner heuristics to prevent a noisy client from forcing Band A status.
- Privacy: don't persist raw user text for non-annotated probes; store fingerprints and embedding hashes.

Testing & rollout plan

1) Staging-only shadow run (2 weeks): enable CF+DPG in shadow leaving production decisions unchanged. Collect metrics.
2) Canary rollout (5% of probe volume): enable gating decisions for non-critical slices. Monitor detection precision and budget.
3) Gradual promotion (25%, 50%, 100%): ramp up with pause points and automatic rollback thresholds: precision < 0.82 or budget > 1.15x for 24h.

Audit & reproducibility

- Persist the gating policy version and policy_id with every probe event.
- Store replay checkpoints every 12 hours for 30 days to enable deterministic replay for triage.

Appendices

A. Example hedged routing JSON (for the router service)
{
  "slice_id": "SLC-2025-42",
  "probes": [
    {"variant": "base", "sample_fraction": 1.0},
    {"variant": "quant-8bit", "sample_fraction": 1.0}
  ],
  "explain_tags": ["hedged:confidence-0.52", "reason:ambiguous-band"]
}

B. Example annotation contract for human review
- Minimum context provided: prompt id, model version, top-3 token probabilities (optional), deterministic seed, and anchor label.
- Annotator task: label whether response is "acceptable" | "unsafe" | "incorrect" with brief rationale.

C. Related telemetry panels (dashboard IDs)
- CF_BAND_DISTRIBUTION: dash-3371
- HEDGED_AGREEMENT_RATE: dash-3410
- PROBE_BUDGET_SPEND: dash-3499
